# Source-side notes from the loan KB audit (agent aa0e6f894a3051bf3), round 1 — verdict task0=PASS task1=PASS — copied verbatim by the coordinator

**Source-side and cross-product notes (no effect on the verdicts)**
1. The source rules list the parts of the repull charge and the application fee by name. The KB spreads them across the factor documents; I lose nothing at the level of meaning.
2. The task 1 lock extension of 2026-10-13 has 5 of its 10 days borne by Larkspur, but its cost bearer is the borrower. Neither the source nor the KB defines a partly Larkspur-borne extension; the record's cost-bearer field settles it here.
3. The short-notice credit counts from the day the Closing Disclosure is prepared, but it is dated the next business day. Both dates give the same tier here.
4. The Hometown Heroes fee-discount doc says "not one the customer states on the call". The task 1 caller says he is an ER nurse, so the line bears on the task. I judged it a restatement of the source's "verified occupation" rule, not a red, but you may want to weigh it.
5. Cross-product, appraisal: the appraisal product retires its own "update charged the reinspection fee" clause. The loan doc's appraisal update line still reads the report type's reinspection fee from the tariff, so there is no contradiction, but a reader could be tempted toward the appraisal product's own update charge.
6. Cross-product, lock: the lock product books Larkspur waivers against borrower-paid extension charges. The loan lock-cost and lock-exclusion rules say nothing about a waived extension. Nothing in task 1 triggers this, so it is an untested gap.
